sentences.text: Oh, hey, can you hear me?
Hi.
Yeah.
Oh, there we go.
Sorry, I'm just connecting the hands for you one second here.
Awesome.
Nice to meet you, Andy.
Yeah, nice to meet you, Ryan.
How's things going?
Very well, you know, seasons are changing, things are.
Christmas time's coming.
It's a nice vibe.
How are you?
Yeah, exactly that.
It's getting very autumnal.
Whereabouts you base?
You're in Canada.
Yeah, I'm in Toronto.
It's probably as cold as it is here.
You're in, in England?
I am, yeah.
In the uk just outside of London by about an hour and a half.
So yeah, not too far from London.
Nice.
Have some family in Bournemouth.
Oh yeah, Bournemouth, yeah, yeah.
Brilliant.
Small world.
Yeah, yeah, definitely, yeah.
Well, Matt invited me to this call.
I took your website, really like it.
We're always looking for marketplaces and you know, people that are buying and selling businesses.
This is great.
Yeah.
Be good to understand a little bit more.
Obviously we have a marketplace so any listings that you'd like to look of, you just need to go through the normal process there.
But be interesting to find out what you guys are doing and whether we can help you in any other ways.
Definitely, yeah.
There we go.
I can hear you.
I can hear you guys better.
Okay, can you guys hear me now?
Sorry about all of that.
You can.
Yeah, yeah.
So it's a little bit.
I'm sorry, go on, Matthew.
Oh no, I just.
I had a crying baby in the room where my laptop was, so I gotta move to the office.
Okay.
Yeah.
So just a little bit about us.
We're M and a advisory for marketing services businesses.
Majority of our clients are either agencies or private private equity looking to acquire marketing agencies.
We work both on the buy and the sell side.
Our sell side platform you obviously seen sounds like anyway agencies.go where we list agencies for sale and then on the buy side we.
We do off market searches for.
For our clients help them to acquire multiple agencies sometimes so but certainly to speed up the process to acquire businesses.
So I see you guys are making some acquisitions.
You've got a 200 million target, have you?
To acquire a bunch of businesses and then list on the stock market.
That's correct, yeah.
So we're a Canadian holdings company and we're operating in six countries.
Our subsidiaries are in Latin America, Europe, Dubai, United States.
And we're trying to expand quite a bit using some debt and some equity.
So a lot of, a lot of the deals we take are partial cash, partial equity in the holdings company napkin.
And the idea is that napkin as a common stock NPKN will, when go, when it goes public will be around $50.
And so it's like a lot of the founders, if they're larger size founders, they typically are required to stay on with us to the event of an ipo.

And then if they're smaller, we just buy their companies and we let the subsidiary management take them over so we can look at things like adjusted ebitda which becomes relevant in that it's true cash flow post acquisition and those will just pay out in full.
So founders will, you know, typically get what they're asking for with some nominal shares, you know, maybe something small that we buy back over time.
So it depends, you know, we're looking for only cash flowing things.
So we don't, we're not really venturing in the sense like we're more private equity but we're not backed by LPs, we're backed by ourselves and debt providers, institutional debt.
So there is an investment bank, Canada's largest investment bank that backs us as well.
So they'll book run when we go public and whatnot.
But everybody that is on our side is looking for cash flow.
So when we scan listings, you know, we know pretty much all the brokers in America.
But when I found you, I was like, oh cool, this is, this is awesome.
We need, we need this over in Europe too.
And we're actually looking at also buying a very large broker.
I shouldn't say who, but it sort of opens the thought of like, well what if Napkin Deals owns a bunch of brokerages around the world too?
Then we can cherry pick the best listings.
That's just a secondary thought, I'll throw that out there anyways.
But yeah, I'd love to get to know your portfolio and yourself and if you have some good stuff.
We're very serious and we have an acquisition in London that we want to do.
It's a fintech and if that happens then it opens the doors big time.
Yeah.
So we are based in London.
Majority of our business is actually in the US so probably 99% of our clients are US based.
We do have UK based clients but we're kind of international in that respect.
We just sold an agency, which is an Israeli agency to an American holding company.
So we sort of work right across the board.
Any English speaking country really.
We're probably in it to some degree.
Yeah, I mean sort of the listings that we have at the moment, I mean it really just depends obviously.
I don't want to waste your time, just sort of listing stuff out because it's all there to see.
So I mean it really depends what type of agency you're after.
Obviously our clients are looking to be acquired mostly cash deals.
They're all, all different sizes.
Some are relatively small, others are, you know, probably worth 30, 34 million.
So it's quite varied stuff that we have on there.
What is your criteria for an acquisition?
You know, do you have size, geography or is it just, you know, are you looking people for people to be part of the roll up strategy or.
Cash flow first minimum 300,000 in free cash flow.
So if it's like adjusted EBITDA, you're probably looking at 5 or 600,000 like brass tax, real cash flow, at least 300.
That's because we borrow for the smaller deals and we need to pay back for a hurdle rate.
So and then, you know, if it's a smaller deal, we pay out some of our subsidiary managers to operate.
So and then we.
Agencies are fine.
We have Napkin Creative, we have Napkin Tech as well.
I can, Ryan or I can send you a catalog of all the divisions that we have.
We have five or six divisions.
The agency still well with us.
We are looking for bigger stuff too.
So I'm not sure.
I haven't looked at all the listings on your site, but I've looked at a few and I see a lot of like 1 in 2 million.
I didn't see any really big ones.
But also never, never sure if you know, pocket listings.
Sometimes brokers like yourself have, you know, stuff that's not able to be shown or whatever.
But you know, ideally we would just scan everything and then plug it into our system.
Ryan's built a pretty good engine.
He's sort of engineer by trade and I'm loving what I'm seeing.
Ryan's the director of M and A.
That's why I wanted him on the call because he would get familiar with your catalog and then, and then click forward this stuff to the board that I sit on with four others for decisions.
And yeah, I mean agencies are perfect, right?
So if that's what you have, that's totally in our wheelhouse.
I see.
Great alignment.
Yeah, great.
So I mean, it's difficult.
So understand what it is exactly you're looking at.
Obviously all of our clients both buying outside, they have sort of ideas about where, where they want to end up or what they're acquiring.
So it wouldn't usually just be based on ebitda, it would be, you know, we're looking for agencies that do a certain thing I mean, how many agencies have you, you got already?
You've got the napkin creative, you said.
Have you acquired any other businesses?
Yeah, so we're, we've done about a dozen now.
We're, I think we're on our 12th deal now and we have about 23 or 24 teed up to acquire.
We've just onboarded a pretty large sized debt provider that can scale up to, you know, a couple hundred million in debt.
So if, you know, if you consider some stock being taken from founders, in some, some cases we can double the size of debt, you know, using some shares and acquire, you know, a lot more.
But buy in from founders is great, right?
It's like a freebie, right?
If someone wants to take our shares, that's amazing.
Right.
And we also do really believe in that.
Like we started this thing on the private side at 19 cents a share.
We're around $3 now just from having six or seven rounds over and over.
But I mean, that's not the first focus though.
Like first is just cash flow.
And that's why we use brokers, because it's hard to find ourselves.
Right.
Like guys that actually want to sell, that have sufficient profit because we're not trying to be a venture deal.
So a lot of ideas out there and we need vetted things and just give you a sample.
Like we bought SEO agencies, PPC agencies in the past.
Amazon Marketing we're very familiar with.
We have not bought any e commerce businesses yet, but we're interested in that if we have the right agencies that we can just start firing clients and buying our own e comm businesses.

So agencies that are really good at e commerce is interesting for us tech shops as well, like agencies that work on the conversion rate optimization or have some hand in handling gross merchant volume for larger clients.
We love agencies with good sort of Fortune 500 client bases.
That's important to us.
Although we have today a lot of high profile customers through the companies we own, we always love more.
Right.
And geographic regions would be great, you know, if we bought some stuff in Europe that had some of the same clients we have in us.
That's a recipe for growth.
We got Gatorade, Procter and Gamble, Nike, Domino's Pizza, Mercedes, Renault, some of the bigger stuff.
But those are clients mostly in Latin America and some in the U.S.
like Harvard Staples, I think a couple more.
But yeah.

So anything that we can bridge our services geographically, it might be a good look for us for some of our larger clients to say, oh wow, napkin, you're now in, you know, London and Spain and Netherlands.
We just opened up in Spain and Netherlands, but yeah.
Ryan, am I missing anything here, buddy?
I just want to make sure.
No, I think, yeah, that covered it really well.
Like, yeah, anything that can really service these digital companies.
Like, we even looked at podcast companies, right?
We've looked at.
Sometimes we do look at SaaS companies.
Like, if we find like.
Like example, in the past, we looked at this company that had like an SEO SEM sort of SaaS offering.
Right.
So it can help our portfolio companies and the clients that they have.
Right.
Yeah, I mean, we've got some interesting stuff.
So we've got a B2B PR company that we're just about to list, based in Miami.
I think.
She did.
That's awesome.
Yeah, about 1 million EBITDA.
Probably looking for a 5 or 6x somewhere around there.
And she's very well known.
I think she's got 500,000 followers as well.
So she's a bit of an influencer herself.
The owner probably looking to stay in, depending on the business that acquires her.
We've got a large shopper media SaaS platform, which is the one I mentioned before, probably worth about $30 million.
Yeah, we're in the process talking some big holding companies, but I wouldn't.
I wouldn't assume that they would be the right fit for you guys.
Just very, very large business.
And they want to go into a holding company probably with a bit more track record, you know, a lot.
Yeah.
Money are holding, you know, big holding companies where they can settle in for the long term and hide, probably.
We've got.
Just to give you a idea of size, too, just to be transparent, top line, we're looking around 35 million consolidated EBITDA, around 10 for napkin.
So that's.
That's where the.
That's the.
Where we are on the path.
If we acquire the rest of the stuff in our funnel, we'll be around 100 million and about 26 in EBITDA.
So, yeah, like, some of the bigger deals are too big to bite off, but we are looking at a $44 million transaction right now in the payment space.
So if that goes through, I mean, the institutional funding is there now it's just a matter of does the cash flow make sense?
And it's a little harder to find big stuff like that where the cash flow makes sense, you know, sufficient to pay back the debt.
So just if you find any sort of gems like that that are high, EBITDA 5, 6, 7 million, that would be phenomenal.
We can handle those for sure.
Yeah.
Okay.
I mean the listings are there.
By all means, let me know what you're interested.
I mean it's easier for us as an organization if you just sign the NDA and then it would just go through the process to get you in front of the founders.
But you know, just as an idea, we've got a lead gen company that just works exclusively with franchise companies or franchise owners, should I say.
We've got a, an E commerce content company that generates huge amounts of content for Amazon products.
They work with some really big brands doing that.
We've got lots of lead gen stuff, B2B lead gen as well as like full service marketing, digital marketing agencies as well.
So I mean it's all kind of awesome.
It's all, it's all there.
All right, that's awesome.
That's a gem.
And you said most of your clients are in US but when you said that, I just want to confirm that that's not the buyers, that's the actual sellers.
Right.
We work with buyers and sellers.
So not only are we working with the majority of businesses that are based, but most of the transactions we do are in the US anyway, regardless of buyers or sellers.
Okay.
So yeah, I mean it's just a, it's a big market, English speaking market.
Obviously we're dealing with Canada as well, but, but beyond that it's just, it's mostly UK and a little bit of Europe and Middle east stuff.
So I mean it's fairly, it's fairly broad the, the areas that we cover.
But in terms of like actual deals that we get done, it usually ends up having an American on one or both sides of the transaction.
So.
Those Yankees, man, I tell you, they just gobble everything up.
I've got all the cash.
I'll throw this out, I'll throw this out there.
Just scale 1 to 10.
Like how convicted would you be on, on selling your brokerage if offered to merge in with four or five other large brokers for like a super play?
Would that ever appeal to you?
Cash on the table.
Fair enough.
Yeah, fair enough.
Well, it would, it would have to be a big cash offer, but I certainly wouldn't want to be sticking around working for other people.
It's not the sort of thing that I do.
So yeah, I'm not, I'm not really looking for it.
I know there is a large brokerage in the US agency brokerage that are looking to exit soon.
So I'm sure you're talking to those.
Guys already, which I won't say who it is, but if you do, I will.
I might nod and smile.
We'll see.
Yeah, we'll see.
I wouldn't, I wouldn't want to say.
We've had a lot of large agencies talk to us about the same thing.
Obviously, cherry picking.
We do actually have investors in the business already who are agency owners that bought into the company, obviously believe what, what we're doing.
But in terms of selling that out to be part of a bigger agency group, I mean, for me it would have to be a lot of cash and a clear exit path.
I'm in my 50s and not looking to stick around, be told what to do.
So no problem.
Fair enough.
But just for the record, we tell no one what to do.
We're more of a holdings than a operator.
But hey, on the cash side, we'll get our bag up first a little bit more and we'll see how this next year shakes out.
If we can get past that 100 million, I think we can do it on the revenue side.
And if so, then we'll have a lot bigger cash offers available for people.
But you just seem like a good guy.
No, we've had so many of these calls, man, that just, they, they're run around the bush and they don't talk about the meat.
It's just all fat and bones.
So I feel like this is a great call, I mean, the way that.
We work with buyers.
So I mean, maybe this is something from further down the line because it sounds like you've got a lot of deals in your pipeline already.
But what we do is we work with buyers.
We just accelerate the entire process for you.
We've got a database of 130,000 agencies there in our CRM.
We've got 20,000 subscribers to the Agencies Co newsletter as well.
So we're pretty networked.
Including our managing director who's actually based in San Francisco.
He's like 30 years in M&A, the last 10 just doing agency deals.
So we've got some good contacts out there.
And what we do is we go out, we find targets for our clients, we bring them to the table.
Usually we have like a senior advisor on board as well who's an expert in whatever field it is that you're looking to get into.
So somebody who's been a COO or CEO of a fairly large or influence or influential agency before, and then we're able to bring those deals to the table really quickly.
We've had a really good run working on deals on the buy side.
We just Work with a company called Skyview.
They're based in Miami.
Miami, New York actually.
And they have done two transactions with us in 10 months, which is pretty quick.
But private investors like yourself now at 4 million EBITDA after those first two.
Deals, so could I.
Oh, sorry, I thought you were down there.
That's all right.
Could I ask.
I know Ryan's probably gonna go nuts scanning all the listings.
Just off the top of your head, do you have anything.
We had a deal fall through just a couple weeks ago that was 5 million EBITDA and that was already pre financed.
We had a term sheet and everything.
And it was a kind of a heartbreaker.
The guy got a twice as big offer from someone else and our offer was 15 million in cash.
Do you have anything on your list in the 5 million plus EBITDA range that we could swap out and just take a look at like I'll.

Ryan would look at it literally today and we'll sign an loi and because we have a call on, on a Thursday with our financial partner, one of them and it'd be cool to just say hey, we found another one.
We literally don't have a replacement for it.
You'd be shocked how many, how few 5 million plus EBITDA deals there are.
Yeah, no, I mean we work on the buy side so I know it's difficult to get those conversations be taken seriously enough at the top level as well.
We don't have any that we have the mandate for that I can think of that would be a good fit.
But certainly we have them in our database.
So Skyview, who we've just done the two deals with, we've been talking to agencies, over 5 million EBITDA as well.
So we do have some fresh conversations.
But obviously we, we don't represent them.
So if we were to the table, it would be.
Our win fee would come from your side for doing the deal.
So we'd have to have a mandate.
How much would it do?
Do you charge on the buy side or you just charge on the sell side?
We charge on both sides.
So we have retainers on the, the buy side.
So 5,000 US a month retainer and then we take one and a half percent on the deal as well.
And that's if you're like signed up or if I'm just scanning listings, is that, do you pay the 5,000 too just to be able to scan the.
Listings or if you're scanning listings, that's fine.
Now what we do is we bring like two or three screened leads Every week for our clients.
So yeah, we're going out and doing the legwork for you.
So this is all off market stuff.
So we're talking to loads of people at any given time and then if we find somebody that's ready to sell, it's got a good business.

And obviously we're having those conversations on behalf of our client, arranging meetings and then we meet with our clients on a weekly basis and we're running through, you know, where we are in the pipeline and arranging calls for them so that they can get in front of these founders.
But I guess that's what Ryan's doing for you already.
So I don't want to take his job away from him.
Yeah, just, I don't know.
Ryan, what do you think about 5k in the budget for having some 5 million plus EBITDA deals?
I guess I got both of you.
How confident are you could bring that three or four of those?
Because if, if you are, I mean I could probably squeeze budget for that.
Depends.
The one and a half percent is more important probably than the five.

Okay, well the, I mean the one and a half percent has never been a problem for us in terms of like when you're getting your debt sorted, they're usually happy with brokers or bankers fees they're used to pay, paying them all, budgeting for them.
So that part of it's not usually a big deal.
In terms of the 5k a month.
Yeah, I mean 5 million EBITDA, there's less of them.

So realistically we could probably get those, but we could only last like a couple of months and then it would start to slow down significantly just because there's not a ton of those deals out there at any given moment.
But it may well take a few more months to sort of eke out all of the good ones.
I mean, it's on our side.
We're doing, is we, we're constantly generating loads of marketing to, you know, put opportunities in front of our, our mailing lists.
And then when we get somebody who's interested in a certain offer, obviously then we're engaging with them and bringing them in.
So it just really does, does vary on a weekly basis.
So that's great to hear about the process.
So with that 130,000 database of companies, do you have like data points on them as well too?
Like you do have revenue or it's more like this is what I think it could be and then you kind of like drip communication to them to like.
So yeah, it's a combination.
We don't have data on every single business, but we do have somebody that works pretty much full time that's adding deals and data points to the database as we go.
So, yeah, we're collecting.
I mean, my.
Me and my team probably speak to 100 plus agencies a month and all of that data goes in.
We're collecting all via AI as well.
So that's all going into our CRM and we're able to search CRM via keywords and various data points so we know what people are buying at and what they're looking for in terms of a deal as well.
So that's all in there?
Yeah.
That's great.
All right, sweet.
I have the info I need on my side.
Appreciate that.
Any questions you have remaining, Ryan?
No, I think that's.
Yeah, that answers it all.
And appreciate it.
Yeah.
Well, good to meet you both.
Sounds like you're doing really well already and it's a great mission that you're on, so be good to hear any updates if we don't speak for a while.
But Ryan, just.
If you engage with any of those listings, that'll be a member of my team most likely to pick up that conversation.
So the process usually assigned an NDA and then they will shop that to our client.
Once the client approves the potential buyer, then we will share the SIM or the im, whatever you call it, and then set up a call with our founders.
So that's the usual process.
If you get on it could be a deal to be done.
That's awesome.
You'll definitely be hearing from us.
Thank you, Andy.
Okay.
Nice to meet you.
Enjoy the rest of your day.
You do.
Speak soon.
Cheers.

summary.overview: In the Business Development and Potential Partnership Discussion meeting between Matthew Liberto and Andy Day, participants introduced themselves and provided an overview of their respective organizations, with Andy detailing his company's M&A advisory services targeted at marketing agencies and Matthew discussing Napkin's acquisition strategy focused on agencies with a minimum of $300,000 in free cash flow. The meeting highlighted Napkin's current portfolio, which includes around 12 completed deals and a pipeline of 23-24 more, with a consolidated EBITDA goal of $100 million, while expressing interest in sectors such as SEO, PPC, e-commerce, and tech agencies with Fortune 500 clients. Andy presented potential collaboration opportunities, including specifics on prospective deals, while outlining his company's fee structure for buy-side services. Action items were assigned, with Ryan tasked to evaluate potential deals and Matthew considering budget allocation for Andy's services, indicating a mutually beneficial prospect for future partnerships.

Andy detailed his company's expertise in this niche, while Matthew shared Napkin's acquisition strategy, emphasizing their interest in agencies generating at least $300,000 in free cash flow. They explored collaboration opportunities, with Andy presenting specifics on potential deals and outlining his fee structure for buy-side services.
